newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue-chips end lower on thinner volumes.
newsitem.headline: KL blue-chips end lower on thinner volumes.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks closed on a weaker note on Tuesday as foreign fund managers remained sidelined, said analysts and dealers.
Weak performances on the Thai bourse, the run up to the UMNO party elections and the end of the third quarter, were all cited as reasons for the weaker sentiment in Kuala Lumpur, they added.
"Fund managers are generally happy with their ratings on Malaysia at the moment," said an institutional dealer in Singapore.
The Composite Index closed down 5.42 at 1143.08

"Foreign funds are waiting and seeing at the moment before redeploying funds from Thailand after it hit almost a three-year low on the stock market yesterday," said Faez Khairuddin, head of research at SJ Securities.
Traded volume on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) stood at 2.23 million shares. Losers outpaced gainers 366 to 219.
Stock broker K & N Kenanga made a fairly dissappointing debut on the KLSE, said analysts. The newly-listed stock closed the day at 3.86 ringgit after an initial offer price of 2.50 ringgit.
